newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles higher as specs cover shorts.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles higher as specs cover shorts.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed firmer as speculative short-covering carried prices off the recent lows hit on Monday, dealers said.
The new-crop December contract settled at 75.64 cents a lb, up 0.71 cent. Spot July ended up 0.42 at 72.66 cents.
Speculators, who maintain a sizable net short position, are expected to continue to cover positions ahead of the July contract's expiry on June 24.
As of early Monday, open interest in July stood at 22,613 lots, down 1,509 lots from the previous session.
Trade scale-up selling could cap gains around 76.00 cents in the December contract, but floods and rain in the Delta could provide some support for new-crop futures, analysts said.
Players await the U.S. Department of Agriculture's revised planted area estimate on June 30, which is likely to prompt changes in the next supply and demand report, released in July.
Private analyst Sparks Cos. today pegged planted area at 13.89 million acres for the 1997/98 season, compared with the USDA's March estimate of 14.48 million acres.
Sparks pegged harvested area at 13.13 million acres versus USDA's 13.25 million acres, and output at 18.137 million 480-lb bales compared with USDA's 18.5 million bales.
Volume was estimated at 13,000 lots compared with Monday's official 20,941 lots.
